customManagers.description: dist's own version sits in [workspace.metadata.dist], and the cargo manager only reads dependency tables — without this it is tracked by nothing and silently falls behind. The Dockerfile declares it a second time, because the dev image installs the dist that regenerates release.yml and it has to be that same version; matching both here means one pull request moves them together.

packageRules.description: The dev image's base tag floats within a major (rust:1-slim picks up new minors on 'docker compose build --pull', matching how CI floats on dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable), so only the major needs a pull request. Grouping it keeps the Dockerfile and compose file in one change.
compose.yaml names the locally built dev image so all four services share one build. It is not published anywhere, so there is no registry for Renovate to look it up in.

A dist bump is only half an upgrade: the version is also baked into the installer URL in .github/workflows/release.yml, which dist generates and verifies byte-for-byte at release time. Renovate cannot run dist to regenerate it, and the incomplete pull request still passes CI — the release only fails later, after promotion to master. Hence the note on the pull request itself.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ **Incomplete on its own.** `.github/workflows/release.yml` still installs the previous dist, and dist verifies that file byte-for-byte at release time, so this branch releases nothing until the workflow is regenerated. On this branch, run:

```sh
docker compose build
docker compose run --rm shell dist generate
```
then commit the rewritten `release.yml`. CI passing does not cover it — nothing in the gate reads `release.yml`. `docker compose run --rm shell dist generate --check` verifies the result.
